baseSteps.title: Check for injuries and safety hazards
baseSteps.detail: Call 911 if anyone is hurt or if the roadway is unsafe. Many insurers require a police report number when you file a claim.

baseSteps.title: Gather official documentation
baseSteps.detail: Request the crash or incident report from responding authorities and note badge numbers. Most insurers will ask for this reference number.

baseSteps.title: Notify your insurance company promptly
baseSteps.detail: Most policies require notice within 24 hours or as soon as practicable. Reporting quickly helps avoid delays or denied benefits.

liability.title: Share liability details
liability.detail: Liability coverage pays for damage or injuries you cause to others. Provide your insurer with the other parties' contact, vehicle, and injury information so they can coordinate payments.

liability.title: Confirm state minimums
liability.detail: Ask whether the claimed losses exceed your liability limits. If so, your adjuster can explain additional options such as personal umbrella coverage.

collision.title: Schedule an appraisal
collision.detail: Collision coverage usually requires an inspection by an approved adjuster or repair facility. Ask about virtual estimates or drive-in centers in your area.

collision.title: Verify rental reimbursement
collision.detail: If you have rental car coverage, request approval before booking a vehicle so the daily limits are documented.

comprehensive.title: Document non-collision damage
comprehensive.detail: Comprehensive claims often require photos of weather, animal, theft, or vandalism damage along with any police reports or witness statements.

pip.title: Track medical expenses
pip.detail: Personal Injury Protection reimburses medical bills and lost wages regardless of fault. Keep invoices, receipts, and disability notes to submit for reimbursement.

medpay.title: Submit medical bills promptly
medpay.detail: Medical payments coverage has lower limits than PIP but can pay for co-pays and deductibles. Provide itemized bills within the time limit stated in your policy.

uninsured.title: Collect proof of uninsured status
uninsured.detail: Gather statements from the other driver or police notes confirming lack of insurance. Many states require a sworn affidavit before uninsured motorist benefits are released.

rideshare.title: Confirm app status
rideshare.detail: Rideshare companies provide different coverage depending on whether you were waiting for a request or had an active trip. Capture screenshots of your trip logs to share with the insurer.

injury.title: Request medical records
injury.detail: Hospitals can provide discharge summaries and billing statements that most insurers require when evaluating injury claims.

property.title: Collect repair estimates
property.detail: Most carriers accept two to three written estimates from licensed repair facilities. Upload them through your claim portal or share with your adjuster.

multiVehicle.title: Exchange complete information
multiVehicle.detail: Multiple vehicles increase liability questions. Gather each driver's policy number, insurer, and statement about fault for the adjuster.

singleVehicle.title: Document road and weather conditions
singleVehicle.detail: Photos of icy roads, potholes, or fallen trees help confirm a single-vehicle loss was unavoidable.

theft.title: File theft verification
theft.detail: Provide the police theft report case number and any recovery updates. Many insurers will not finalize payment until the waiting period in your state expires.

bike.title: Coordinate with health insurance
bike.detail: Cyclists may need to use health insurance first and then coordinate subrogation with the at-fault driver's insurer. Ask your adjuster about reimbursement procedures.

pedestrian.title: Review state PIP eligibility
pedestrian.detail: Some no-fault states allow pedestrians to claim PIP benefits from the vehicle's insurer even without owning a car. Ask which forms are required.

documentChecklist.title: Documents most insurers request
items: Photos or video of the scene and damage
Contact and insurance details for other parties
Medical bills, wage statements, and receipts
Proof of ownership or loan/lease documents

insurers.name: Allstate
insurers.notes: Have your policy number and the incident date ready when calling.

insurers.name: GEICO
insurers.notes: GEICO's mobile app lets you upload photos for Express Services.

insurers.name: Progressive
insurers.notes: Ask about scheduling a Service Center appointment for repairs in select cities.

insurers.name: State Farm
insurers.notes: You can also reach your local State Farm agent for help starting the claim.

insurers.name: Farmers Insurance
insurers.notes: Farmers allows online claim tracking once you register for a My Farmers account.
